title: Psalms Chapter 79 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 79 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 79 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 79.

questions.question: Who is the psalmist of Psalms 79?
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:1 begins with 'A Psalm of Asaph,' indicating Asaph is the psalmist.

questions.question: What have the heathen done to God's holy temple according to Psalms 79?
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:1 states that the heathen have defiled God's holy temple.

questions.question: What is the condition of Jerusalem described in Psalms 79:1?
questions.explanation: The verse says the heathen 'have laid Jerusalem on heaps,' describing destruction.

questions.question: According to Psalms 79:2, whose dead bodies are given to be meat unto the fowls of the heaven?
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:2 says the dead bodies of God's servants have been given to the birds.

questions.question: In Psalms 79:2, the flesh of whose saints is given to the beasts of the earth?
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:2 mentions the flesh of God's saints given to beasts of the earth.

questions.question: What have the enemies shed like water round about Jerusalem in Psalms 79:3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:3 states their blood has been shed like water around Jerusalem.

questions.question: According to Psalms 79:3, what was lacking for the dead bodies around Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: The verse says there was none to bury the dead bodies.

questions.question: How have the people become to their neighbors according to Psalms 79:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:4 says the people have become a reproach and scorn to their neighbors.

questions.question: What question does the psalmist ask the LORD in Psalms 79:5?
options: How long wilt thou be angry forever?
When will the temple be rebuilt?
questions.correctAnswer: How long wilt thou be angry forever?
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:5 asks 'How long, LORD? wilt thou be angry for ever?'

questions.question: In Psalms 79:5, what does the psalmist say might burn like fire?
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'shall thy jealousy burn like fire?'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 79:4 says the people have become a blessing to their neighbors.
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:4 says they have become a reproach and scorn, not a blessing.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 79:3, their blood was shed like water around Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:3 says their blood was shed like water round about Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 79:2 describes the dead bodies of the heathen given to the beasts of the earth.
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:2 describes the dead bodies of God's servants and saints given to fowls and beasts, not the heathen.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 79:5 contains the psalmist's plea asking how long the LORD's anger and jealousy will last.
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:5 asks 'How long, LORD? wilt thou be angry for ever? shall thy jealousy burn like fire?'

questions.question: In Psalms 79, which event is mentioned first?
options: The people becoming a reproach to neighbors
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:1 mentions the heathen defiling the temple before other events.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 79 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 79 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 79:6, on whom does the Psalmist ask God to pour out His wrath?
options: The heathen that have not known God and kingdoms that have not called upon His name
The people of Israel who have sinned
The priests who defiled the temple
questions.correctAnswer: The heathen that have not known God and kingdoms that have not called upon His name
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:6 specifically asks God to pour out His wrath on the heathen and kingdoms that have not known or called upon His name, highlighting the judgment on those who reject God.

questions.question: What has happened to Jacob and his dwelling place according to Psalms 79:7?
options: Jacob has been devoured and his dwelling place laid waste
Jacob has been saved and his dwelling place restored
Jacob has been honored and his dwelling place blessed
Jacob has been scattered but his dwelling place remains
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob has been devoured and his dwelling place laid waste
questions.explanation: Verse 7 declares that Jacob has been devoured and his dwelling place has been laid waste, symbolizing destruction and suffering of God's people and their land.

questions.question: How does Psalms 79:8 express the Psalmist's plea regarding former sins?
options: To remember not former iniquities and to show tender mercies quickly
To punish all former sins severely
To ignore all pleas for mercy
To repeat the sins as a lesson
questions.correctAnswer: To remember not former iniquities and to show tender mercies quickly
questions.explanation: Verse 8 asks God not to remember former sins against His people but to show tender mercies speedily because they are brought very low, emphasizing repentance and dependence on God's mercy.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Psalms 79:9 for asking God to help and deliver His people?
options: For the glory of His name and for His name's sake
For the wealth of the nation
For the power of the king
For the honor of neighboring peoples
questions.correctAnswer: For the glory of His name and for His name's sake
questions.explanation: In verse 9, the plea to God to help, deliver, and purge away sins is motivated by the glory of God's name, showing that God's reputation is intimately connected to His salvation of His people.

questions.question: According to Psalms 79:10, why should the heathen not question the whereabouts of God's people’s God?
options: Because God will be known among the heathen by revenging the blood of His servants
Because God has abandoned His people
Because the people have hidden God from the heathen
Because the heathen worship the same God
questions.correctAnswer: Because God will be known among the heathen by revenging the blood of His servants
questions.explanation: Verse 10 requests that God reveal Himself among the nations by avenging the blood of His servants, preventing the heathen from questioning God's presence or power.

questions.question: What does Psalms 79:6 teach about the relationship between knowing God and experiencing His wrath?
options: Those who do not know God or call upon His name are subject to His wrath
God’s wrath is poured out on His own people only
Wrath is unrelated to knowing God
questions.correctAnswer: Those who do not know God or call upon His name are subject to His wrath
questions.explanation: Verse 6 links God's wrath with those who have not known Him or called on His name, teaching that rejection of God leads to divine judgment.

questions.question: How does Psalms 79:8 demonstrate the virtue of humility in prayer?
options: By acknowledging their low condition and asking God to remember not their former sins
By blaming others for their troubles
questions.correctAnswer: By acknowledging their low condition and asking God to remember not their former sins
questions.explanation: The verse shows humility by confessing lowliness and pleading for mercy rather than demanding it or justifying themselves, reflecting a contrite heart.

questions.question: What practical lesson about forgiveness can be drawn from Psalms 79:9?
options: That God’s forgiveness is connected to His glory and the purity of His name
That forgiveness is optional for believers
That forgiveness is only for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: That God’s forgiveness is connected to His glory and the purity of His name
questions.explanation: Verse 9 teaches that God’s forgiveness serves His own glory and is essential for His name’s sake, encouraging believers to seek forgiveness as part of honoring God.

questions.question: What will happen according to Psalms 79:10 if God is made known among the heathen by revenging the blood of His servants?
options: The heathen will no longer question where their God is
The heathen will increase their mockery
questions.correctAnswer: The heathen will no longer question where their God is
questions.explanation: Verse 10 implies that a visible act of divine justice will silence doubts about God’s power and presence among the nations.

questions.question: Which biblical virtue is exemplified by the plea in Psalms 79:9 to 'purge away our sins'?
questions.explanation: The request to purge sins reflects repentance and a desire for spiritual cleansing, important virtues in Christian living.

questions.question: According to Psalms 79:7, what is the consequence of the heathen's actions against Jacob?
options: Jacob is devoured and his dwelling place laid waste
Jacob prospers and his dwelling is secure
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob is devoured and his dwelling place laid waste
questions.explanation: Verse 7 clearly states the destruction suffered by Jacob and his home due to the heathen’s actions, emphasizing consequences of hostility.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 79:8 asks God to speedily punish the people for their former iniquities.
questions.explanation: Verse 8 actually asks God not to remember former iniquities but to show tender mercies quickly, indicating a plea for mercy not punishment.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 79:6 teaches that God's wrath is poured out on those who do not call upon His name.
questions.explanation: Verse 6 explicitly asks God to pour out wrath on the kingdoms that have not called upon His name, affirming this teaching.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 79:10 encourages the heathen to say, 'Where is their God?' as a sign of doubt.
questions.explanation: Verse 10 actually asks God to prevent the heathen from questioning where their God is by revealing His power, not to encourage doubt.

questions.question: What does Psalms 79:9 suggest will accompany God's help and deliverance?
options: Purging away of sins for God's name's sake
questions.correctAnswer: Purging away of sins for God's name's sake
questions.explanation: The verse links deliverance with cleansing from sin, highlighting spiritual restoration alongside rescue.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 79 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 79.

questions.question: According to Psalms 79:11, what is requested to come before God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:11 specifically requests that 'the sighing of the prisoner come before thee,' highlighting a call for God’s attention to the suffering of captives.

questions.question: In Psalms 79:12, what is the measure of retribution requested to be rendered to their neighbours?
questions.explanation: The verse uses the number seven, a number of completeness and divine judgment in Hebrew thought, requesting neighbors to receive 'sevenfold' their reproach, emphasizing full and just retribution.

questions.question: What metaphor is used in Psalms 79:13 to describe the people of God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:13 calls the people 'sheep of thy pasture,' a common biblical metaphor denoting God's care and guidance over His people as a shepherd over sheep.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the theme of pleading for God's vengeance on the enemies as seen in Psalms 79:10?
questions.explanation: Psalm 94:1 similarly calls on God to 'avenge the blood of thy servants,' directly paralleling the plea in Psalms 79:10 for God to be known among the heathen by avenging His people.

questions.question: What is the significance of the word 'jealousy' in Psalms 79:5, considering its Hebrew root meaning?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'jealousy' (qanna) in Psalms 79:5 conveys God's protective zeal for His covenant relationship and holiness, not human envy, emphasizing His righteous anger against defilement.

questions.question: What literary device is demonstrated by the parallel structure in Psalms 79:2 ('The dead bodies... meat unto the fowls... flesh unto the beasts')?
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:2 uses synonymous parallelism by repeating the idea of the dead being given as food to different creatures, intensifying the horror of the desecration.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 79:8 asks God to remember former iniquities against the people.
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:8 explicitly says 'O remember not against us former iniquities,' requesting God to forgive past sins rather than remember them.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist in Psalms 79 asks God to preserve those appointed to die according to His power.
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:11 petitions God to 'preserve thou those that are appointed to die,' highlighting a plea for divine mercy even upon the doomed, according to His great power.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage contains a similar lament regarding the destruction of Jerusalem and defilement of the temple as in Psalms 79:1?
questions.explanation: Lamentations 2:6 describes the Lord abandoning His altar and destroying His sanctuary, paralleling Psalms 79:1’s lament over the defilement of the holy temple and Jerusalem’s ruin.

questions.question: What is the historical context implied in Psalms 79:7 where it states 'For they have devoured Jacob, and laid waste his dwelling place'?
options: The return from exile in Persia
questions.explanation: The verse alludes to the Babylonian destruction of Jerusalem, when foreign nations devastated the land of Israel ('Jacob') and its temple, consistent with the psalm’s tone of national calamity.

questions.question: In Psalms 79:9, for what purpose does the psalmist ask God to help and deliver His people?
options: For the glory of thy name
For the wealth of the nation
For the peace of the kings
For the comfort of the widows
questions.correctAnswer: For the glory of thy name
questions.explanation: The psalmist appeals for help and deliverance 'for the glory of thy name,' indicating that God's reputation among the nations is at stake, not merely the people's welfare.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of forgiveness and purging of sins found in Psalms 79:9?
questions.explanation: 1 John 1:9 promises that if we confess our sins, God will forgive and cleanse us, paralleling Psalms 79:9’s plea for God to 'purge away our sins.'

questions.question: What does the plea in Psalms 79:6 to 'Pour out thy wrath upon the heathen' reflect about the psalmist's understanding of God's justice?
options: God’s righteous judgment against the unfaithful
questions.correctAnswer: God’s righteous judgment against the unfaithful
questions.explanation: The psalmist calls for God’s wrath against those who 'have not known thee,' reflecting an understanding of God as a just judge who punishes nations that reject Him.

questions.question: Which literary structure is evident in Psalms 79 when the psalmist moves from lament to petition and finally to thanksgiving (verses 1-5, 6-12, 13)?
questions.explanation: The psalm is framed by lament at the beginning and thanksgiving at the end, creating an inclusio that brackets the psalm with contrasting emotions and focuses the reader on God’s ultimate deliverance.

questions.question: What is the significance of the number seven in the phrase 'sevenfold into their bosom' in Psalms 79:12?
options: It symbolizes completeness and divine retribution
It refers to seven years of punishment
It represents the seven days of creation
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes completeness and divine retribution
questions.explanation: In Hebrew culture, seven often symbolizes completeness or perfection, so 'sevenfold' implies full and perfect retribution for the reproach given by neighbors.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 79 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 79 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What specific divine attribute is primarily expressed in the plea found in Psalms 79:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 79:5 directly refers to God's jealousy burning like fire, indicating the attribute of divine jealousy in response to sin and defilement.

questions.question: According to Psalms 79:9, what is the primary reason the psalmist asks for deliverance and cleansing?
options: For the sake of the people
For the glory of God's name
questions.correctAnswer: For the glory of God's name
questions.explanation: The psalmist prays for help and cleansing specifically 'for the glory of thy name,' emphasizing God's honor as the motivation (Psalms 79:9).

questions.question: What theological doctrine is exemplified by the request in Psalms 79:8 to 'remember not against us former iniquities'?
questions.explanation: This verse expresses a plea for God to forgive past sins, directly relating to the doctrine of forgiveness (Psalms 79:8).

questions.question: How does Psalms 79:3 illustrate the severity of Israel’s suffering in the context of divine judgment?
options: The land was flooded by water
Blood was shed like water with no burial
The enemies were victorious in battle
questions.correctAnswer: Blood was shed like water with no burial
questions.explanation: The verse describes bloodshed 'like water' around Jerusalem and the absence of burial, highlighting the extreme devastation and disgrace (Psalms 79:3).

questions.question: What does the psalmist identify as a consequence of the nations’ actions in Psalms 79:7?
options: They have devoured Jacob and laid waste his dwelling place
They have embraced the God of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They have devoured Jacob and laid waste his dwelling place
questions.explanation: This verse states that the nations have destroyed Israel’s people and their land, indicating the physical and spiritual devastation caused by their enemies (Psalms 79:7).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted by the prayer in Psalms 79:11 concerning the prisoners?
questions.explanation: The verse calls on God to preserve prisoners 'according to the greatness of thy power,' emphasizing God's omnipotence (Psalms 79:11).

questions.question: How does Psalms 79:1 connect to the broader biblical narrative of God's covenant people and their land?
options: It shows the permanent possession of the land
It records the defilement of God’s inheritance by heathen nations
It celebrates the building of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: It records the defilement of God’s inheritance by heathen nations
questions.explanation: Verse 1 describes heathen nations defiling God's inheritance—the temple and Jerusalem—highlighting covenantal breach, a theme throughout Israel’s history (Psalms 79:1).

questions.question: What combined theological truth emerges from Psalms 79:6 and Psalms 79:12 about God's response to enemies?
options: God ignores the heathen and urges forgiveness
God’s wrath is poured out and He repays reproach sevenfold
God blesses the heathen and protects the innocent
questions.correctAnswer: God’s wrath is poured out and He repays reproach sevenfold
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 12 together show that God’s wrath is poured upon unrepentant nations and that He repays reproach upon His people sevenfold, emphasizing divine justice (Psalms 79:6, 12).

questions.question: What does Psalms 79:4 reveal about the social consequences of Israel’s suffering?
options: They became a blessing to neighboring nations
They were a reproach and object of scorn to neighbors
questions.correctAnswer: They were a reproach and object of scorn to neighbors
questions.explanation: Verse 4 describes Israel as a reproach and derision to their neighbors, indicating social disgrace resulting from their calamity (Psalms 79:4).

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about God’s justice and vindication is synthesized from Psalms 79:10 and Psalms 79:12?
options: God ignores the mockery of the heathen
God will vindicate His people and repay reproach against Him
God’s people must seek revenge themselves
questions.correctAnswer: God will vindicate His people and repay reproach against Him
questions.explanation: Verse 10 requests God to be known by revenging the blood of His servants, and verse 12 calls for sevenfold repayment to neighbors who reproach God, highlighting divine vindication (Psalms 79:10, 12).

questions.question: Considering Psalms 79:13, what is the expected response of God's people after deliverance according to this psalm?
options: They will give thanks forever and proclaim God's praise
They will rebuild the temple alone
questions.correctAnswer: They will give thanks forever and proclaim God's praise
questions.explanation: Verse 13 expresses the commitment of God's people to thank Him forever and declare His praise to all generations following deliverance (Psalms 79:13).

questions.question: How does Psalms 79:2 contribute to the understanding of the gravity of Israel's plight in this chapter?
options: It shows the enemies' respect for the dead
It depicts the dead bodies of God's servants given as food for birds and beasts
questions.correctAnswer: It depicts the dead bodies of God's servants given as food for birds and beasts
questions.explanation: Verse 2 graphically describes how the dead bodies of God's servants were left for birds and beasts, highlighting the utter disgrace and suffering (Psalms 79:2).

questions.question: What apologetic response does Psalms 79:10 provide against the skeptic’s claim that God is absent or powerless in times of Israel’s suffering?
options: God is absent and silent in suffering
God will be known by revenging the blood of His servants, showing His active presence
questions.correctAnswer: God will be known by revenging the blood of His servants, showing His active presence
questions.explanation: This verse counters the skeptic by affirming that God will be revealed among the nations through just vengeance for His servants’ blood, demonstrating His active sovereignty (Psalms 79:10).

questions.question: What does the psalmist imply about human helplessness and divine power in Psalms 79:11?
options: Human strength is sufficient for deliverance
Only God’s great power can preserve those doomed to die
Prisoners can save themselves through prayer
questions.correctAnswer: Only God’s great power can preserve those doomed to die
questions.explanation: The verse requests God to preserve prisoners 'according to the greatness of thy power,' emphasizing human helplessness and dependence on divine omnipotence (Psalms 79:11).

questions.question: What combined theological understanding about sin and restoration can be drawn from Psalms 79:8 and Psalms 79:9?
options: Sin is ignored and restoration is unnecessary
God’s mercy and salvation are sought to overcome the consequences of sin
Restoration depends solely on human effort
Sin has no effect on God’s people
questions.correctAnswer: God’s mercy and salvation are sought to overcome the consequences of sin
questions.explanation: Verse 8 pleads for mercy and to not remember past iniquities, while verse 9 asks for salvation and purging of sins, together teaching the need for divine mercy and salvation for restoration (Psalms 79:8, 9).
